title: Efficient Distributed Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Enhancing Language Model Performance
datasets: WikiText2; WikiText103; 10k_prompts_ranked; Wikipedia Dec 2018 dump (~21M docs)
models: Qwen2.5-1.5B; OPT-1.3B; Contriever; DPR; ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2 reranker; Faiss
hardware: Cloud: Xeon Silver 4210R, 64GB, RTX 3090; device: MacBook Pro i7, 16GB, no GPU
key_result: DRAGON achieves up to 1.9x greater gains over the standalone SLM compared to centralized RAG, and a 42.4%-49.5% reduction in per-token latency compared to synchronized methods under 300 ms network latency.
notes: Device-cloud split: private docs stay on device, cloud holds public corpus. Evaluated mainly via perplexity on WikiText; single LAN testbed; 15.6-20.3% higher per-token latency than device-only. Last ~12k chars of page unread.

title: EncouRAGe: Evaluating RAG Local, Fast, and Reliable
datasets: HotPotQA; FeTaQA; FinQA; BioASQ (24,968 QA pairs, 51,068 documents)
models: Gemma 3 27B; multilingual-e5-large-instruct; Jina v3 and MiniLM-L6 v2 rerankers; Chroma; vLLM
key_result: Hybrid BM25 attains F1 of 40.8 (HotPotQA), 50.1 (FeTaQA), 51.8 (FinQA) and 49.9 (BioASQ), versus Oracle Context at 43.4, 49.4, 72.9 and 54.5.
notes: Framework + empirical comparison. Reranking adds 2-4x time with marginal gain. Single generator. Repo anonymised. Numbers taken from fetcher summary of Table 3.

title: Enhancing Legal LLMs through Metadata-Enriched RAG Pipelines and Direct Preference Optimization
datasets: PrivacyQA (194 QA); MAUD (1,676 QA); Australian Legal QA (DPO, 150 test)
models: LLaMA 3.2 1B Instruct (DPO); LLaMA 3.2 3B (LoRA, appendix); gte-large; Gemini API (metadata/summaries)
key_result: After DPO alignment, refusal on the correct-context set drops to 1.5% (from 53.2%) while refusal on incorrect context rises from 87.3% to 99.3%.
notes: Local small model but metadata/summaries use external Gemini API (privacy not evaluated). BERTScore only; text/table mismatches in span recall; no code link; no p-values reported.

title: Evaluating an On-Premises Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Health Records Retrieval: Retrieval Performance, Response Latency and Perceived Usability in Kenyan Level 5 Hospitals
datasets: Synthetic health-record corpus (1,603 chunks); 12 curated queries, 6 classes
models: Phi-4 Mini Instruct 3.8B (generator); Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (local judge)
key_result: The naive baseline outperformed both advanced configurations on key-fact context precision (0.687 vs 0.633 and 0.591) and was the only configuration meeting the 30-second target (mean 13.99 s vs 34.33 s for the no-rerank ablation).
notes: Very small eval (12 queries, 13 users); synthetic data; low-prestige journal (IJRPR), verify peer review. Source verifiability rated by users (partial citation). Hardware not stated in abstract. Full-text PDF fetch returned empty.

title: Evaluating Biomedical Reranking for LLM-Based Question Answering over Longitudinal Clinical Notes
datasets: 1,000 QA pairs over notes of 200 bariatric surgery patients
models: PubMedBERT (dense); BM25; MedCPT cross-encoder; Qwen3-8B generator; local judge (unnamed)
key_result: Reranking increased Hit@10 from 46.6% to 60.6% and MRR from 0.2371 to 0.3252, while judge-assessed answer correctness rose from 44.8% to 48.6%.

title: Evaluating RAG Performance on Small Language Models for Low-Resource Devices through Chunking and Retrieval Methods
datasets: 148 Indonesian questions from official Hajj guidebook
models: Small language model on Android (not named in abstract); dense/sparse/hybrid retrievers
key_result: Sparse retrieval with 256-token chunks and 100-token overlap yields the best answer quality (F1 = 0.726), while 128-token chunks with the same overlap give the fastest generation time (69.737 seconds).
notes: DOI landing page gave abstract-level info only. Single domain/dataset. Indonesian language.

title: Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation Variants for Clinical Decision Support: Hallucination Mitigation and Secure On-Premises Deployment
datasets: 250 de-identified patient vignettes
models: Twelve RAG variants incl. Haystack (DPR+BM25+cross-encoder), RRF hybrid, self-reflective RAG; specific models not reported
key_result: The best retrieval accuracy (P@5 >= 0.68, nDCG@10 >= 0.67) was achieved by a Haystack pipeline (DPR + BM25 + cross-encoder) and hybrid RRF, while self-reflective RAG lowered hallucinations to 5.8%.
notes: MDPI returned 403; abstract only. Security (encryption, provenance, audit) is proposed protocol, not evaluated.

title: Grouping-Aware Numerical Verification for Offline Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering over Institutional Documents
datasets: Constructed 15-case numeric extraction benchmark; 20-case verifier set; random-vector index scaling (1k-50k)
models: 6-layer distilled sentence-transformer (384-d); FAISS flat L2; Ollama quantised 1B and 3B instruct models; Tesseract OCR
hardware: Virtualised Intel Xeon 2.80GHz, 4 logical cores, 15.7GB RAM, Linux
key_result: The baseline extractor is exact on 5 of 15 cases versus 15 of 15 for the grouping-aware extractor, and baseline precision falls to 0.833 on the 20-case verifier set; mean retrieval latency reaches 10.55 ms at 50,000 segments.
notes: Answers withheld if numerals unsupported; end-to-end latency, retrieval quality and verifier recall on real output marked TO BE MEASURED; self-authored constructed benchmarks; no actual LLM in evaluated loop

title: HalluGuard: Evidence-Grounded Small Reasoning Models to Mitigate Hallucinations in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
datasets: FineWeb-derived HalluClaim (86,024 triplets); LLM-AggreFact incl. RAGTruth
models: HalluGuard-4B (Qwen3-4B, LoRA+ORPO); Llama-3.3-70B; Qwen3-32B; Mistral Large 2; GPT-4o judge
key_result: HalluGuard-4B reaches 75.7% average balanced accuracy on LLM-AggreFact (+1.9 over Qwen3-4B backbone at 73.8) and 84.0% on RAGTruth, matching MiniCheck-7B.
notes: Hallucination detector, not a retriever; release promised upon acceptance (not yet available); synthetic training data, English only
